records.subject: MUS
records.title: Class Guitar
records.description: Class instruction on basic guitar; repertoire will be selected from classical, jazz, rock, pop, fusion, and world music.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Music Fundamentals I
records.description: Notation and performance of music fundamentals: pitch, rhythm, scales, key signatures, and intervals.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Music Fundamentals II
records.description: Notation and performance of music fundamentals: melody, rhythm, scales, intervals, key signatures, triads; preparatory for MUS 251.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Understanding Music
records.description: Introduction to understanding music from aesthetic, cultural, and historical perspectives; music ranging from the earliest folk and art music traditions to modern popular music and beyond is listened to and discussed, all from a global perspective.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Survey of Music Literature
records.description: Exploration of predominantly western music through demonstrations, performances, lectures, concerts, and discussions.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: World Music
records.description: Exploration of music from a global perspective through demonstrations, performances, lectures and discussion.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Introduction to Music Technology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 151 or 251, or concurrent enrollment in either.
records.description: Music notation software, audio recording and editing, and music specific web design.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.title: Class Piano I

records.description: Pedal, sight reading, transposition, playing by ear, chord progressions, melody harmonization and improvisation.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Class Piano II
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 181.
records.description: Scales, arpeggios, blocked and broken chords; repertoire to complement individual skills, theoretical knowledge and improvisation.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Introduction to Music Education
records.description: Introductory course for principles and practices fundamental to music learning and teaching, as well as analysis of the connections among learning theories, human development theories, and educational practice in today's music PK-12 classrooms.

records.description: Exploration of the complex and changing world of the entertainment industry including contracts and negotiations, professional organizations and networks, and industry standards.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Fundamentals of Music Entrepreneurship
records.description: Techniques of self-promotion, including social media, web design, and marketing for the creative product.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Materials and Structures of Music I
records.description: An examination of the fundamentals of music theory; pitch, rhythm, scales, intervals, and chords.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Applied Theory I
records.description: By examination. Ear training, conducting, rhythmic reading, sight singing, keyboard, dictation.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Materials and Structures of Music II
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 251 with a C or better; MUS 252.
records.description: Analysis and composition of diatonic and initial chromatic harmony, figured bass, two-voice counterpoint, and phrase structure.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Applied Theory II
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 251 with a C or better; MUS 252 with a C or better.
records.description: Ear training, sight singing, keyboard.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Music Composition
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 251 or concurrent enrollment.  By Interview Only.
records.description: Original writings in small forms.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Applied Jazz Theory and Improvisation I
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 251 and 252 with a C or better.
records.description: Applied study of fundamental jazz theory and improvisation concepts including rhythms, four-part chords, modes of the major scale, ii-V7-I progression, harmonic minor scale, guidetones, 12-bar blues form, and blues scales.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Applied Jazz Theory and Improvisation II
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 257 with a C or better.
records.description: Applied study of intermediate jazz theory and improvisation concepts including five-part chords, modes of melodic minor scale, chord-scale theory, idiomatic jazz progressions, voice-leading, rhythm changes, bebop blues, and bebop scales.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Rock Music: History and Social Analysis
records.description: History and analysis of rock music related to its African American origins, its societal role, and its diverse development and impact.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Rags to Rhinestones: A History of Country Music
records.description: History of Country Music from its humble roots in Appalachian folk music, Black American spirituals, the blues, and other immigrated cultural traditions to the modern age of Country musicians selling out arenas all over the world.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Music Technology I
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 164.
records.description: MIDI hardware/software and related technologies used in music production. Sequencing, orchestration, virtual instruments, sample control, interactivity, performance.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Native Music of North America
records.description: Music and ceremonialism as a reflection of realities in North American native cultures, past and present. (Crosslisted course offered as MUS 265, CES 271.)

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Film Music
records.description: The evolution of film music; discussions/lectures will address aesthetics of film music and how they influence perception, communication, and drama.

records.subject: MUS
records.title: Black American Music: Roots to Fruit
records.description: A critical survey of key musical and societal forces contributing to today's African American musicscape; listening, analysis, and critique.

records.title: Applied Theory IV
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 351 with a C or better; MUS 352 with a C or better.
records.description: Continued development in ear training, sight singing, keyboard and dictation, emphasizing 20th century music.

records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MUS 251 with a C or better; MUS 252 with a C or better; ENGLISH 101 with a C or better.
records.description: History and style of western art music from Antiquity to 1650; introduction to and selected topics in ethnomusicology.

records.description: History of jazz in chronological sequence; social and political contexts of the African-American origins of jazz; stylistic developments.

records.description: Exploration of music through the lens of LGBTQ+ representation as a way of examining the personal and social struggles the community has endured for decades. (Crosslisted course offered as MUS 366, WGSS 366.)
